utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, good afternoon everybody. Good afternoon to you, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. All the accused are present. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Vanderpuye. The floor of the Defence teams or amongst the Defence teams, I notice the absence of Mr. Nikolic, Mr. Bourgon, and I think that's it. Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. Did you manage to go home for the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are going to proceed and hopefully finish with your testimony today. If I remember well, we had started your cross-examination, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Your Honours, I have started it, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So let's proceed with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Last we think we started discussing some of your report and you shared with us a couple things, and I didn't get an answer to a question. You told me last week that you are not well versed in military terminology, that was on page 27999. You told us that you were not a military expert, same page, line 7 through 8. You also shared with us that you didn't see or receive any reports from the police, that's again at page 28001. And then, with respect to the facts that you really are testifying about Srebrenica and some of the orders in July of 1995, you told us that, "You only have knowledge of an average person following the media." And that's on page 28007, lines 18 through 21. And finally, you shared with us that you really didn't know when an enemy offence started or ended, same page, 28007, and then again you repeat at page 28009 at line 10, that you don't know all the facts. Now, I asked you last Friday, what expertise do you have, and I don't believe I got an answer to that question which appears on page 27999. So to be fair to you and to really to understand your report better, can you tell us in your words what expertise do you have given the foregoing that I just highlighted for you?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you last asked me this question, whether I knew when a military offensive starts and ends and that is how I understood your question, and in those terms I believe that I said that I wasn't the man who is familiar with military terminology in the sense that I do know what an offensive is; but however, when it starts or when it ends I am not able to tell that to either you or the Chamber because I am really not familiar with military terms; and therefore, I cannot be helpful in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, what expertise do you have, sir? That's really all I need.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you like to -- to tell me -- tell you what my CV says about that? I teach criminal law at the Faculty of Law in Novi Sad, that is in the Republic of Serbia. I also teach an optional subject of international law, and I have the title of assistant professor in that particular domain. So as I said, this is the basic level of university tenure in the Republic of Serbia. I don't know what else you are interested in, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well I did get a chance to read your CV, and I do have a couple of questions with respect to that. You state that you were the advisor to the prime minister of Republic of Serbia in 2007, and then you have a hyphen. Are you still the advisor to the prime minister?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, when did that end, sir?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either in 2007 or 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I acted as an advisor on two occasions, and I think that it ended in April or March this year. I am not sure. It was in the spring of 2008 when I finished my duty as an advisor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And that was for Vojislav Kostunica, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Vojislav Kostunica was the prime minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you ever in an organisation called Obraz, O-B-R-A-Z?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know of that organisation. I read about it in the media in Serbia, but I have never been a member of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I have some information, maybe you can confirm or deny it. I understand that you ran for a candidate for the mayor of Novi Sad in the last election; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I ran for the mayor of Novi Sad, in my city of Novi Sad; and that was in the spring of this year in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I understand from just reading, and when we Googled, you, we found some things, and for example, you were involved in an incident involving -- on April 11th, actually, where you storm through an information stand and tore up posters and propaganda material that was relate to the ICTY. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. Do you really think that this has something to do with me. Is that what you're implying?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, if my colleague could repeat his question. I believe that will he received the wrong translation to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, on moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may help the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment Professor, and you, Mr. Ostojic. Mr. Lazarevic, what's the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think that the translation we received was improper in relation to the this incident that allegedly happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is precisely why I have called upon you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers kindly not speak at the same time for sake of interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry about that. Could you explain to us where the translation is faulty, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It said, "you were involved in an incident," this is what my colleague said and this is not what was translated. It was translated to the witness, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm still not understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I think we can clear it up if I can just show him a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but there has ban a wrong translation and wrong interpretation, and we need to know exact what it consists of. And we start from there; and, of course, I'm sorry for the interruption in your cross-examination, but this needs to be cleared up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I can explain very clearly. It wasn't translated to the witness that he was personally involved in an incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's the reason why I intervened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But what we have in the transcript is essentially correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the transcript is correct but the translation was a bit wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So, Professor, what I am going to do and then Mr. Ostojic will beef it up, if necessary. I am going to read out to you his question, and then, of course, you will be given all the opportunity to reply. The question as we have it in the transcript, which I understand was not completely translated to you runs as follows: "And I understand from just reading, and when we Googled you, we found some things; and, for example, that you were involved in an incident involving on April the 11th, actually, where you stormed through an information stand and tore up posters and propaganda material that was related to the ICTY. Is that accurate?" Now, before you answer, I will let Mr. Ostojic confirm whether he wishes to clarify this further and add anything or change anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, I think it's acceptable the way you read it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So yes, the ball is in your Court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understood the question, eventually. And I never took part in any such incident and to tell you, honesty, I don't know about such incident taking place at all. I believe given the date that the election campaign was in progress at the time; but, however, I really do not recall any such incident taking place in Novi Sad at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I will show you a document, but before I do you remember a woman by the name of Jelena Gregoric, who was the chairperson of the Liberal Democratic Party and having been attacked and brutality beaten on April 8th in Novi Sad?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know her. I know that her party did take part in the election, but I don't note this particular lady.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me just quickly, and it's a minor point, but just quickly so you can see it to be fair to you. I am going to show you an article which states that it's from the Lawyers Committee For Human Rights, captioned: "Human rights and democracy violation early warning weekly news letter number 6," and on the bottom it says: "Supported by open society institute." And with the Court's permission if the usher can hand witness the B/C/S version and place on the ELMO the English version, we will be directing everyone's attention to paragraphs 6 and 7. This is the B/C/S and this would be the English.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there is my name here says that I burst in, and I tore down the posters on the wall. And this is something attributed to me under item 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you don't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. A man from another party called New Serbia was the perpetrator. Do you want to know his name?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Previous topic. Maybe my topic can clarify where's mentioning of the ICTY in this? Because it was suggested to witness that some propaganda material related to ICTY was destroyed by this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's actually a follow-up to my next question. I should have broke it up, but first I wanted to know if he was involved in that incident on the 11th, and, in fact, the propaganda material.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Although you claim that you weren't involved in it, sir, are you familiar with the fact that the propaganda material was material to the ICTY and this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what's the gentleman's name that was involved in this incident?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rade Bastar.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which party? Of which party.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Novi Serbia, New Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I think that I am done with this document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before you say you are done. It's still a little bit unclear to me how such a mistake could happen in a document like this. Is there a reason behind all this that you could advise us of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, there was a reason. I was an eyewitness of the incident. I don't know if somebody put my name purposefully within the context of what had happened. I cannot say for sure. It is a mistake. This document that Mr. Ostojic has shown me is something that I had never seen before. However, if he had browsed through the press and the newspapers printed on that day, he would have learned the truth. And it happened at the crossroads called Merkator in Novi Sad if that is of any pertinence to the whole incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I move on, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I still don't believe, and I am sure the Court will correct me if I am wrong, you shared with us what you what your CV and educational background is. But I want to know concretely in this case having reviewed although limited documents, what is your expertise? You are not here as a military expert, and we understand that you are an associate professor of law and you studied law, and we accept that. What is your expertise, then?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I told you I teach international criminal law at the Fault of Law in Novi Sad. I don't know if I should go into the syllabus of all the subjects that I teach. I don't know what else I can add. I can now, however, give you an example. The OSCE branch in Serbia, when they want to engage someone to deliver a lecture to the judges or prosecutors for war crimes in Belgrade, they engage me. Would you really believe that they would do that if I were a person who is in contempt of this sort -- of this court, who were tearing up the material and the propaganda material relating to this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I let -- you talk a little bit about resubordination. Is that an area of expertise that you maintain that you have, the issue of resubordination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the issue of resubordination is in relation to the laws regulating it. So I think it would be fair to just say to the witness this, because I do believe that this is something that is regulated by law, and he was the one who analysed legal regulations in Republika Srpska, which is clearly explained in his expert report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it makes much difference the way we are going, so Mr. Ostojic and Professor, please proceed. You have heard in any case what Mr. Lazarevic had to say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have. What I said last time I can repeat now. I am not a military expert, but I do believe that in a certain sense I am qualified enough to interpret legal instruments, particularly those relating to criminal responsibility. And I do believe that I am an expert in that area; however, it is an unthankful task to speak about one's self. It is up to other people to say whether they are qualified or not qualified. I don't think it's appropriate for me to speak about my achievements and qualities. Sir, did you have any objections to my training and qualification when I was accepted as a witness? If you didn't have any objections at that time, I don't see why we have problems now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay, let me ask you this, sir. With respect to this order of the 10th of July 1995 that you reviewed where the task was signed by the President Karadzic, and ultimately ordered by Mr. Kovac, to: "Crush the enemy offensive," and you've explained quite thoroughly, repeatedly, in fact, that you don't know what the term "offence" means, so I'm I am not asking you that. But did you learn or obtain any information whether that goal, which was supposed to be precise and specific as you outlined, was it ever modified at any time subsequent to the 10th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you think if I saw any legal document that he is talking about, my answer is no, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did you learn any information from any source whatsoever whether that July 10th, 1995 precise and specific purported resubordination assignment of the special MUP to the Drina Corps, whether or not that was ever modified?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you think that I have seen the document relating to this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, because they always object, so I am trying to break it down as simply as possible for you. First I asked if you saw any document and you gave us an answer to that. Now I am asking you if you learned from any source from either the lawyers or from other witnesses --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at P60, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: While we are waiting for this, I forget to mention earlier on today that we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis. Judge Kwon's absence is due to some official business that's attending to and that we will continue to be sitting in this day until the end of the week. He will be back with us on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, now you have P60 in front of you and it deals with the 12th of July, 1995. And you remember last week we listed out those five specific units of the MUP that were going to be considered as special police brigade that was purportedly going to be resubordinated to the Drina Corps. Here in this specific order of the 12th of July, or report I should say, it identifies the 5th Company of the Zvornik CJB as being involved in such tasks relating to the Muslim column that was passing through Susnjari, et cetera, towards Tuzla, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we look at the first order --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, I think that my colleague should be a little bit more careful, because he said that, "MUP that were going to be considered as special police brigade," this is not what the document says. This is not what the evidence says. Only one part, one unit within this unit was a special police brigade -- only part of the special police brigade. It was a special police detachment, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's clear enough. I think it's clear enough such that we can proceed. Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you look at this document, P60, they add another unit or whichever term you like to use, although I hesitate to use the military terms because I know that you are not that familiar with them. But if they add the 5th Company of the Zvornik CJB to this, is that something that is separate and apart from the special units that were assigned on the 10th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, let me read this. I've not seen it before. Very well. I have read the document. Now, what was your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: This 5th company of the Zvornik CJB --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- was not resubordinated to the Drina Corps or any VRS unit, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only tell you who was subordinated -- resubordinated to the Drina Corps according to Order 6495 and whether any other units were subordinated to the Drina Corps pursuant to any other orders. I don't know, because I've not seen any such orders. This order, 6495, implies only the units that are mentioned in here as being subordinated to the Drina Corps. That's the way I understand this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And the 5th Company of the Zvornik CJB was not, correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think that the witness already answered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 64/95, the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that, sir. I know we can all go back and read that. I just wanted to know if you know. Now, who is ordering this 5th Company of the Zvornik CJB to perform certain combat tasks, activities or operations? And just take a look at P60 and I think you'll find the words, "I have ordered" in the last paragraph, and then you can tell us and identify who the person or the author of this report is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's a call for speculation, and furthermore it relates to the previous paragraph, not the last one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I really don't -- I have no response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's move to your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with Dragomir Vasic? Do you know who he is in the context of reviewing this material and preparing this report?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember this name as having seen it any of the documents that I perused. I can't remember. And he is speaking in the first person singular, and you are asking me about the third paragraph of this document where he is, actually using the first paragraph -- first person singular. Is that what you are asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I just asked if you know who Dragomir Vasic was in the context of the issues that you've given us a report on, mainly Srebrenica 1995. Are you tell this Court that you have no idea what his role or function was in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name does not ring any bells. I've not seen this name in any of the documents that I am inspected.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, when you reviewed some of the law, and I know that you didn't look at any of the facts. But you also told us last Friday on page 28005 on lines 10 through 15 that - and it was discussing the issue of resubordination, still, sir - that: "The resubordinated unit is commanded by the military unit..." and you go on, obviously. But in this instance, by looking at P60 and I would like to draw on your expertise if I may, and P60 is on the screen for you. The 5th Company of the Zvornik CJB was actually being command by the chief of the centre of the centre CJB, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just read this once again, please. It seems so. If this, that is mentioned in the third paragraph refers to the second paragraph, but I am -- can't be sure of that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's forget about P60, sir. Because I don't want you to have too much trouble. You're an assistant or professor of law, and you know the law; and you talked about in your introduction the relationships between the MUP and the VRS, just generally speaking from reviewing the law, who does accompany within a centre, hypothetically Zvornik, to whom does it report?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about P60 --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the 5th company?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are speaking in general terms? You are speaking in general terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I am, sir. Just forget about P60 as I said. In the circumstance that we have here, looking at the orders that we have with respect to resubordination, which units were purported resubordinated in July, just reading the law and from your experience and knowledge, to whom would these companies who are within the Zvornik centre CJB, to whom would they report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before you answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that this is not an propriety question for this expert witness. We had an expert witness who dealt exclusively with police issue, reporting within the MUP was a whole chapter in his expert report. And my colleague has a chance to explore this topic in detail with that witness. I don't believe it would be fair with this witness who is not a police expert witness to -- to give answers to these kinds of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic, but it could also be a matter of what the law provides on such matter. So I think the witness can proceed with his answer. It's within what is permissible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In the Law on the Internal Matters and the Law on Internal Affairs and the Law on Immediate Threat of War, I did not see any provisions strictly regulating who is reporting to whom. This is what you have concretely asked me. I have not seen anything to that effect in the law. I don't have any doubts that there are some rules in the police that regulate such matters; however, this was not the subject of my expertise, so I was not looking for those. I don't remember having seen anything about reporting in the Law on Internal Affairs. No such thing have I seen, and I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'll look at that answer again a little later, but just to follow-up on what my colleague Mr. Lazarevic said, you are also not a police expert, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on your definition of a police expert. If you are implying that I am familiar with the work of the police, I would not be able to call myself an expert. However, I can interpret this document if we are talking about the Law on Internal Affairs, if we are talking about all sorts of responsibilities that it provides for, such as disciplinary or criminal responsibilities. But if you are asking me about whether I have ever professionally studied the work of the police, no, I've never done that, and I can't in those terms be called a police expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's take on a look at another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: P886. It's also from this gentleman that you don't what his role is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Although, just to be fair to you. It says on the bottom of his reports that he's the chief of the centre, and the centre would be as we can see in the top page that it was of the Zvornik CJB. Now -- and when that comes up sir, I have a couple of questions in connection with that. Now, we talked about the 5th company and whether or not that company was ever purported resubordinated to the VRS based upon the order of the 10th of July, 1995. I would like to ask you about specifically paragraph 4. It looks as if the chief of the centre of the Zvornik - and I want you to accept it as being true unless you know otherwise - that he is sending on the 13th of July, 1995, a special the detachment to Konjevic Polje from the Srbinje or Doboj units. Do you see that on paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Send a detachment from Srbinje or Doboj to Konjevic Polje, item 4. Is that what you're asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I appreciate you reformulating every question I ever asked. But yes, specifically it is paragraph 4 relating to those two detachments. And I am asking you whether or not these two were mentioned or have you seen any other evidence that they at any time were resubordinated purported to the Drina Corps based on the 10th of July 1995 order?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that this was taken out of context of this document because I think the very beginning of the document says that, "Earlier at the meeting with General Mladic, we were informed that," and then follows 1, 2, 3, 4 -- 4 items. So I believe that this was taken out of context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic. What do you have to say about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't believe that it was taken out of context at all. I think he's an expert here, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, let's simplify it. Do you have the text in front of you? Okay. So that shouldn't be a problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is best placed to know whether it's taken out of context or not. If you feel it's taken out of context and you wish to clarify things, please go ahead and do that first and foremost.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat the question, what are you asking me? Whether these units mentioned under 4 were ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Ever resubordinated to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order, 64/95, does not mention any units that would have anything to do with Srbinje or Doboj. Here a -- an abbreviation is used or a shortened form "special." So I don't know the strength of the unit; however, in document number 64/95 there is no reference to any unit from either Srbinje or Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And who would be ordering like these three units if they were on the scene, 5th Company of the Zvornik CJB, the Srbinje and/or Doboj Special Detachment. Who would be their superior?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the Law on the Implementation of the Law on Internal Affairs, if a police unit pursuant to that law is resubordinated to a military unit in who's area of responsibility it is engaged in combat, if it is resubordinated to it, then it is only natural that the resubordinated unit receives orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is us coming back again to the law again that we have mentioned so many times already.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We have, and you keep going over it, and thank you for that. What if it was not resubordinated? To whom would these three units or detachments be subordinate to? I mean, you have no evidence that they were resubordinated, you shared that with us. You have not seen it. You have not been advised of it. But these three units, just the 5th company of Zvornik CJB, the Srbinje, and the Doboj Special Detachments. Who is their superior? That's all I want to know. You don't have to keep repeating to me that, "if they were resubordinated," I'm telling that you if you haven't read it. There is no order of resubordination who would be their superior in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I can only interpret the law. I can't tell you who they were subordinated to. I only saw this Order 64/95, and as far as the units that were resubordinated according to that order, I can tell you who they were resubordinated to. Under the law if a unit is indeed resubordinated then such a unit will be under the command of the military unit in whose area of responsibility it is engaged in combat. If a unit is not resubordinated, then it has never left the system of command of the Ministry of the Interior. That's how I understand the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And thank you for that, sir. And similarly if a unit that was purportedly going to be resubordinated to the Drina Corps, let's say, in July of 1995, once there is specific and precise tasks -- task ceases or ends, whenever that might be, but we do know what the task was, they also would then go back to be under the command of the MUP. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how I understand the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A police unit that is subordinated. Shall I complete my question -- or my answer, sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let him finish, Mr. Ostojic. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's how I understand the law. While a unit is engaged in combat and performs a task for which it is resubordinated to a military unit. It is under the command of that unit in whose area of responsibility it performs its combat task. When the combat task is accomplished, then the MUP unit goes back under the command of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now let's look at 4D339, if you will.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And as this is coming up, I am just going to ask you, maybe I can draw upon your expertise here. And do you know what the staff of a centre of a police centre is or a public security centre, do you know what that means, the staff of the centre?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staff of the public security centre, you're asking me for a definition of this term? I wouldn't be able to give you one.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know what it even means when think use the term "the staff of the centre"? Do you know what they are talking about?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat. I am not able to give you a legal definition. I can only share with you my assumption. In terms of any precise police terminology or legal terminology, I am not in a position to give you a legal definition of this term.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, maybe I will just still ask you to direct your attention to the bottom portion of this 4D339 exhibit, where it starts in the paragraph before the numerical number 1, 2, and 3. It states: "The staff of the centre has engaged part of its PJP (special police units forces to carry out the following task):" And then it lists three specific things. I understand what you're saying, sir, that you don't have that experience or knowledge or information, but looking at this maybe you can help me out. Does it look as if at this point on July 12th, 1995, that it's actually the staff of the centre of the Zvornik CJB given again that the staff commander, Dragomir Vasic, signed this report, that he's the one issuing orders to the PJP?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understand the Serbian language, the answer would be no. The first sentence is impassive, and the document was signed by the person that you mentioned. If you're using a passive form, then there is no subject. The -- either in the Serbian language or any other language. So this person is not speaking in the first person singular as in the previous document. This sentence does not have the doer, the subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just -- I want to focus your attention on paragraph number 2 or the paragraph that's identified with the numeric 2. It talks about the PJP engaging and setting ambushes in the direction of Srebrenica and securing the Drinjaca-Hans Pijesak Road. Do you see that sir?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you scroll down the document just a little so I can see the whole of it? Yes. Thank you. That's it. I can see that yes, one company has been engaged in pulling up ambushes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know which company it was?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. It says 1, no name, some --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I don't want to -- I don't want to get into too great a discussion with you regarding linguistics and passive usage of words and reports and orders, sir; but if you look at the first and third paragraph where they seem to mention either cooperation and/or coordination with parts of an infantry brigade, the second paragraph doesn't mention that at all, correct? And it basically is giving them this assignment independent of any cooperation, coordination, or assistance from the VRS or any portion thereof, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's take things slowly. You have now established a link between the 1st and the 3rd. Did I understand you correctly? If I understand you properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ristivojevic, let's me ask you this: You don't see that there is a link between the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd with what was said in the paragraph above that. That they were engaging them in the following tasks? You don't think that any of the three are linked?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, three companies are indeed being engaged. I understand that the centre staff is engaging three units under paragraph 1, 2, and 3. Yes. But let me hear your question again. Are you establishing a link between the first and the third paragraph? It says here that the centre staff is engaging three units, but it doesn't say which one. What you are you asking me? Can you repeat your question? Are you establishing a link between the first and the third paragraph? Could you please repeat the last part of your question? I understand that what you're saying is that the staff centre has engaged three units but please repeat the last part of your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I -- one moment, I think we are going too fast. I sense it in the efforts that the interpreters are making to catch up with you. And please slow down, both of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am making a link, sir.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. And your question, the last part of your question, what was it? I have a problem. I have to listen to the interpretation and at the same time, I have to read documents. It takes time. When the interpretations are there. I have to stop and read the document. Please, I am sure you will appreciate that. So can I kindly ask you to repeat the last portion of your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Actually I do appreciate it, sir; and I will give you all the time that you need. First, let me know if you've read the document.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and now, please, your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you look at numeric one and three, you see that there is verbiage there --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- with respect to cooperation and/or coordination for certain tasks, but specifically in paragraph number 2 --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When they are discussing the ambushes particularly in the Srebrenica direction on the road of Drinjaca-Hans Pijesak, it only involves the one company of the PJP, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well, yes, correct. Under 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: To whom is this one company regardless of the fact that you may not know which company it is, to whom is it subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. How should I know? I don't even know what company it is. I only know that pursuant to Order 64/95 which units were subordinated to the Drina Corps, pursuant to this Order 64/95. As for the rest, I can only give you my speculations and say which orders were issued to resubordinate other unit, which units those are. This would be pure speculation on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, do you think setting an ambush has anything to do with crushing an enemy offensive? I mean, clearly you might know the difference between those two orders "offensive" and "ambush"?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me put it this way. If you are asking me strictly in military terms, I've already told you that I can't give you any definitions. I was in the army. I've been through wars. If you're issued an order, you carry the order out. Is your question whether an ambush equals an offensive? Is that your question? I really don't know what to tell you. I believe that you would need a military expert here, somebody who's familiar with the military definitions and military terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's then look at another document, P62.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, maybe that will that might be a little bit easier for us. This is a MUP document or a document, I'm sorry, it's P62, it's a document again sent by the chief of the centre at the Zvornik CJB, Dragomir Vasic, to the MUP RS and police headquarters in Bijeljina. And let me know when you've had a chance to look at this document.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it on the screen yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: They are bringing it up, sir. Just be a little patient. And when you look -- just let me know when you've had a chance to look at it.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I want to just understand how the MUP works, and you've helped us a lot with this resubordination issue when it comes to the VRS. If the MUP is involved in anything the centres within the MUP are subordinate to the minister, correct? Today and probably correct in 1995, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think that the witness already answered this very similar question in relation to MUP and the structure of MUP and responsibilities within the MUP. I mean, going on and on with same kind of questions, I don't think it would be helpful for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what's your comment to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't have a comment to it. I think that it would be helpful and I think it's important if they are going to bring an expert to give evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see. Professor, do you have anything that you think you could add?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so. I was just about to repeat what I said last time. As for strict inner workings of the police and their organisations, I wouldn't dare speak about and call myself an expert in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let's try this topic that you've spent some time giving evidence on, and that's the prisoners of war. Do you know anything about prisoners of war in a general sense from your expertise?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Under what circumstances, sir, would a civilian like a civil commissioner let's say, in July of 1995, under what circumstances would he be involved with prisoners of war, if at all?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A civilian, according to the rules or regulations that I reviewed, there is a document according to which the civilian commissioner was appointed in Srebrenica but with very ambiguous responsibilities assigned to this person. It's called the "Civilian Commissioner for Prisoners of War [as interpreted]." After reading this document and trying to understand it, it does not use any imperative forms of verbs, i.e., ordering the civilian commissioner to deal with the issues of the prisoners of war, but rather uses some more ambiguous verbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay, and are you referencing, sir, Exhibit P24, and if you have it you could tell us and if not we could bring it up, or we should probably bring it up --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one small correction. The witness said civilian commissioner for the municipality of Srebrenica and here it says, "Commissioner of Prisoners of War," just that correction. It's on page 27, line 6 in this transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If that is agreed to, we will proceed. I hear no comments. So the --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think -- I mean, I am sure he is correct on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So the correction will be made in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's on the screen in any event, Mr. Ristivojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's on the screen, I think, or will be soon.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Here it comes. Is that what you're referencing?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can it be scrolled a bit downwards, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And if we could highlight paragraph 4, that might be helpful because that's the one we are trying focus on.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think that's the document that I had in my set, but the content is similar. It refers to the appointment, and it measures the specific name of the person. If you have time, I may try and find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, I don't know that I do.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, here it is. It's P10.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay, well, let's bring up P10, sir. And I know you were starting to describe the passive use and other linguistical terms to describe this specific document. But are you saying that in July of 1995 that the Self-Commissioner Miroslav Deronjic had no authority and no involvement with respect to the prisoners of war that were captured in and around the Bratunac area?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What responsibilities and duties did Mr. Deronjic have on July 12th, 1995, as the civil commissioner with respect to the prisoners of war? List them out for me based on your expertise?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am going to. Item 4 of this order, or, excuse me, decision. It says that the commissioner shall ensure that all civilian and military organs treat all civilians who participated in combat against the army of Republika Srpska as prisoner of war and ensure that the civilian population can freely choose where they will live or move to. What I wanted to say a minute ago when I was speaking was not how you interpreted it. I said that the verb used under Item 4, to ensure that civilian military organs, treat everybody who took part as prisoners of war is rather vague, because it does not say specifically what kind of powers it places on him for dealing with prisoners of war, exactly, that is, precisely, unlike some other documents that speak about, or orders, that speak about military authorities where it is clearly stated who has powers regarding the POWs, and what kind. I say he does have certain powers, but in any view I don't know exactly what they are. And I'm not sure whether you can classify them as some sort of executive powers. And the gentleman appointed on the basis of this decision had a superior power in treating POWs in the municipality of Srebrenica, whether he had the last say and whether his decisions were binding for everyone. If you look at item 5, it reads that "the decisions by the civilian commissions shall be binding for all civilian authorities." So that this word "ensure" mentioned in number 4 does not imply any powers over military authorities regarding POWs as well as other authority vested in the civilian commissioner.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And that's what I wanted to show you P24 that we were looking at earlier, which is an order from Dr. Radovan Karadzic dated the 12th of July, 1995, to the Zvornik CJB. In that particular order on the 5th paragraph, if you will, it says: "Establish close cooperation with Miroslav Deronjic, civil commissioner for the municipality of Serbian Srebrenica as well as with other organs and organisations in the area." What I am asking you is this order was not sent to the militarily as you can see that. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's addressed to the chief of the CJB Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And then, it also directs them to be in close cooperation with Miroslav Deronjic who is the civilian commissioner as we know, and I think as you shared with us previously or last week that he became --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He was appointed on the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. And on the 14th of July, 1995, he got a new position; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what is that position?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the War Presidency of Srebrenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's because a state of war was declared, correct? And prior to that it was only an imminent threat of war, and that's why the titles change, would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are the duties and responsibilities different for a civil commissioner with respect to POWs as they would be for the president of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I have looked at the decision on the appointment of War Presidency issued by the president of the republic, I wasn't able to 25 pinpoint any authorities of the president -- War Presidency relating to POWs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And who can actually direct, let's say, the civil commissioner or even the president of the War Presidency to either move POWs or to place them in certain warehouses? Who would have that ultimate authority? Would that be the Supreme commander?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the civilian commissioner is concerned, he's appointed based on the decision of the president of the republic. And in that way, I believe that once the president of the republic appoints him, because that's what it says under item 2, which reads --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note the witness is ask kindly asked to slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please slow down a little bit because the interpreters are having problems.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I am not sure if you finished, sir. I was looking at another document. Did you finish what you were saying?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as -- as far as. Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's take -- put on the ELMO P1149 A and B. A being the English version and B being the B/C/S version -- I'm sorry, did I say ELMO. I meant in e-court, I apologise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Again, it's P1149 A and B.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And sir, this is an intercept that the Prosecution claims in their evidence between -- they say an intermediary with Karadzic and with Deronjic. And it's dated, from my understanding of what the Prosecution's position is, the 13th of July 1995, a day after the previous exhibit that we were talking about, at approximately 8.10 p.m. or 2010 hours. And take just a moment here to read this rather short intercept, to yourself, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, Mr. Lazarevic, and the witness. This -- I am told that the B/C/S version of this document is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You know, there is a name on the typed version or at least initials, forgive me for not pointing that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For unknown reasons, the English version is not under seal. In any event, in order to avoid any possible miscarriage, I have ordered to have no broadcast of this document. So keep that in mind, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, just let me know what you've had a chance to look at that document and review it.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you scroll it up, please? Yes. Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you seen this document before? Okay. Well, it's a short document. Let's assume for the moment that the Prosecution is correct, that this is a correct intercept between an intermediary of Karadzic's and Mr. Deronjic on the 13th of July, 1995, a day right after the discussion or the order that we saw with the exhibit, prior to that. Do you know what they are talking about there, that they have 2000 and they should be transferred to warehouses and any of that stuff? Do you think you can give us an opinion as to whether or not they are talking about POWs or something else?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, if I attempt to comment any of this, I would totally move from the sphere of facts into the sphere of guesswork, and I don't think that in that way I would be of any assistance to this Chamber. I don't think you need an expert for this. Anyone can read this and then guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I would be trying to go too much into the facts here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think and I seem to have -- my colleagues agree with me on this, that we need to proceed with your next question. I think what the witness has just said is pretty much obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Under the laws that you've reviewed and told us, if the VRS purportedly was in charge of the POWs, can you please explain why Karadzic -- and accept this as being true for the moment - why would Karadzic be telling the civil commissioner where to place POWs? And you can accept this as a hypothetical sir? As an expert I am sure you've had those types of questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does it fall under his expertise, Mr. Ostojic? I don't see it falling under his expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With all due respect to the Court, I'm not sure if it does or doesn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's ask the witness. Do you think it falls under your expertise or is it a question that you can comfortably answer straight forward -- in a straightforward fashion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I cannot. I would be asked to speculate on the facts. We have a decision on the appointment of a civilian commissioner, it's a legal document. This decision was made by President Karadzic, pursuant to the constitution of Republika Srpska. This is where I could be of help; however, I don't think I would be of any assistance to you if I try to make assumptions or guesswork in any other area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay, well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We will. Let's look at Exhibit 5D1389.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And this goes to the topic in your report, sir, of logistics. In your report you talk about how food was supposed to be provided to any unit that was resubordinated, et cetera. So they will bring it up on the screen, 5D1389. And you know, again, I'm sorry, it's the same individual, Dragomir Vasic, and is dated the 5th of August, 1995. And they are talking about diesel fuel and litres of fuel. Can you just help me understand from your expertise, what would a police commander or centre chief be needing this amount of fuel or diesel?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know how this witness can answer this kind of question. This is so factual that it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I -- you know, he should either tell us that -- what's his expertise, honestly? Without being rude in front of the witness, I don't think he's ever answered that just to tell us what his educational background is. He tells us that he wants to look at facts and doesn't want to speculate. Here are some concrete facts for him to draw upon where he can give us a reasonable opinion to the extent that he's able to. I don't believe the objection is sound. I don't believe the witness has been forthright in the answers given. We are giving him specific documents that were introduced into Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop because I think you are abusing of our patience and tolerance, to be honest with you. Can you read your own question, page -- this page 34, lines 5 to 11 and explain to us how this fits in. The expertise on legal matters that this witness supposedly has been summoned to testify upon?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, this witness in his report talks about certain logistics and certain items such as supplies that have to be given purportedly to a special police unit that becomes resubordinated to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but your question is: "What were the police commander or centre chief be needing this amount of fuel or diesel for?"

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's get to your next question. Come on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you, sir -- have you seen this document before? Yes, yes, I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, when we talk about logistics as you do in your report, sir. Is fuel -- diesel fuel or motor fuel, is that also something that would be given to a MUP unit that's resubordinated purportedly to the Drina Corps? Is that something that typically would be provided to them in they needed it?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my report I discuss logistics, in terms Article 14, paragraph 4, on the Law on the Implementation of the Law on Internal Affairs during an imminent threat of war or state of war. So I didn't make anything up. And also on other documents I saw a paper issued by the assistant of the Drina Corps command asking whether he was responsible for the logistics for -- to supply logistics -- logistics supply for the MUP unit resubordinated to him. And he's also asking for certain quantity of dry rations to be provided. So I was mentioning logistical issues only in this context. Please don't take it as if I am an expert in that area as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Trust me I haven't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, when looking at this document it speaks about a fuel for the need of the centre. I really -- I must have, I am puzzled a bit with my colleague's position, whether he claims that all the units were resubordinated, which units were resubordinated, doesn't he claims that the centre was resubordinated to the centre of the Drina Corps. I mean I must say that I am puzzled with the proposition that my colleague is making to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With all due respect to my colleague, he should know that not one of the units was resubordinated because the combat task to crush the enemy offensive never took place. So I think that maybe he could review the document, again, with all due respect to him. But I am going to move on, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And, sir, let me the direct your attention to paragraph 4.13 of your report, which is page 30 in the English version. And there you talk --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What paragraph, again? Can you please repeatedly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sure. 4.13.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am turning the pages. Very well. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now -- now in the middle of that paragraph you state: "According to the available information in relation to this case, the closest camp for prisoners of war was located in a village of Batkovic, the municipality of Bijeljina." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, do I.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What information are you referring to here, sir?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. The location of the camp Batkovici, Bijeljina municipality. Well, it's common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, it may be, sir, but you preface it by saying "according to the available information in relation to this case." All I want to be is what information are you relying on if it's just common knowledge given that your knowledge of Srebrenica is drawn from watching the media as other average people have done at that time. Is that the basis of this?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, when it comes to the territorial jurisdiction of courts, I wasn't able to locate any documents governing that. But I nevertheless drew a conclusion based on what I know. Do you understand? So knowing that this was the closest court territorially, this is what I put in my report and this is how I drew up this conclusion as well. I think I said that at our last session that I hadn't seen the document governing the territorial jurisdiction division among courts, but I did, nonetheless, drew the conclusion. Because I know that geographically Bijeljina and Bileca are closer, and there are military courts well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well have you seen any evidence so suggest that that's where the VRS officers wanted to send the POWs in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Have I seen that in the documents that I examined? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you did see such a document, let's hypothetically say from the Croatian intercept materials that were recently provided to us, that would be consistent with what they were required to do this, is it not? Is to order or send those individuals to the Batkovici camp in Bijeljina municipality, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I know nothing about these intercepts. I am just telling you about what I put in my report. In my view, the POWs must be treated in the following way: First they have disarmed, then taken to a specific area, designated for taking -- giving them over to security guards and then escorted to camp. I had never seen any intercept transcripts from Croatia, and I cannot possibly comment on that. I can only tell you what I saw in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, let me switch a little bit here. You talked a little bit briefly - and this I think is my last topic - about the military Prosecution office and the obligation of people to report crimes. Is there any obligation of the police subordinated or not, or resubordinated or not, to report any crimes that their members were involved in to either the civilian or the military prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SFRY criminal code and the criminal code of the Republika Srpska have certain crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We read that in your report, we know that, we read that.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a general obligation. There is no distinction in these laws. Everybody is bound to adhere to this, whether a policeman or not. Every person is obliged to report a crime and shall be held responsible for failing to report it. The difference is that an official is held responsible and faces a greater sanction and is obligated to report a broader range of crimes. And an ordinary citizen, a narrower range of crimes and his sanction is more lenient.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: To whom would a police commander, let's say, if he learned of a crime committed by his police unit member, to whom would he report that crime to?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of reporting a criminal offence is to provide police with certain information for it to be able to the make a criminal report, go to the Prosecutor, and then launch the whole proceedings. If the policeman whose duty is to file a report, he doesn't have to write anything, he will report to the prosecutor directly. And he is a policeman on duty when the crime was committed. I compiles a criminal report and files it to the Prosecutor. Do you understand? That's the duty of the police --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic. You had asked for one hour. You've been putting questions for over an hour and 45 minutes. You need to finish your cross-examination before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Within the next four minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, just help us, he's supposed to report it to which Prosecutor? The civilian Prosecutor, isn't that right? Yes or no, Mr. Ristivojevic? Is he --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did the police guy have to report it to a civil Prosecutor or to a military prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police do their job. The police do their job, and to the best of their knowledge, because ex officio they are obligated to take into account the jurisdiction, they will report it to the prosecutor who they believe has jurisdiction for this crime. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I really hate to disrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, then tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is Mr. Ostojic talking about any police officer in regular circumstances or he's talking about police -- commander of the police unit resubordinated in combat activities to the military unit in whose zone of responsibility is performing tasks?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, could you clarify that, Mr. Ostojic, and conclude please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think it was relatively clear, and I think we have his ambiguous answer on the record. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Ostojic. We'll have the break now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood your question as being general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So Ms. Nikolic, how much time do you think you will need? Sorry to ask you again, but I think now you could, after having heard Mr. Ostojic's cross-examination and others, you would be in a position to give us a bitter outlook.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. As things stand now, I shouldn't take more than 10 or 15 minutes at the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, good news, Your Honour, on Friday I said it was very unlikely. I can now say definitely not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I hope to be half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We'll have the break now. 25 minutes, thank you. And one moment, Ms. Fauveau, are you in a position to start your Defence case today?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are told, Mr. McCloskey, you wish to address the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We were informed just so -- I don't know within an hour ago, that Mr. Mijatovic, that investigator witness for the Popovic team is apparently here and ready to testify. It's the first we've heard of that, so we just wanted to get an idea of when the plan was that he was going to be testifying. And did you want us to question him or how was that going to work? But, of course, whenever, we just weren't sure what the time-frame was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are ready to -- to hear cross-examination -- to have examination-in-chief with him regarding Hotel Fontana, as you ordered. But if you ordered that -- that it should be done just by the Prosecutor or by the Chamber, we'll comply with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. What's exactly your problem, Mr. McCloskey? Is it that you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No problem, just wanted to know when so we can be prepared to do whatever you want us to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We were surprised as you were, Mr. McCloskey. We were not put on notice -- given no information about the arrival and the availability of this witness today. So we haven't had an occasion to discuss amongst ourselves; and we have only done so now, and as you would have noticed we are short of one judge here today. So however, we believe that the best way to go about it is as follows: You should go first, Mr. Zivanovic, and make it clear to the witness what the parameters are, why he has been recalled, in other words, this is not a total unconditioned reopening of his testimony. It's limited by the subject matter which is the reason why we have asked you to bring him back. Mr. McCloskey will then cross-examine this -- or whoever, I mean, I don't know who, will cross-examine this witness, again limitedly on this area of his testimony. After which, we'll see which questions would like to put, if at all, because I suppose like Mr. McCloskey would like to go back to his previous testimony. And also what prompted us to ask for his re-presentation. Is that agreeable to both of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That sounds fine. Just as I am sitting here thinking about this, just it -- to put you on notice, I seem to recall Mr. Zivanovic in one of his filings said that part of the problem here was a translation issue with -- with the booth. We have reviewed that audio and -- and we have -- I believe we have got a transcript, or I've been told by my people that the translation was -- was pretty good but that there was part of what he had said that was left off the transcript, which we now have a transcript of. I'm not sure we've communicated that with Mr. Zivanovic yet. We can and show him that thing so he can double-check the material. But that's just one other additional issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to inform the Trial Chamber that we asked correction of the translation on 29th September, and it is still is pending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I hope its --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. In any case, let's play it by the ear. We'll see how far we can go with your examination-in-chief, and with the cross-examination, if at all. If you find yourself unprepared for this, Mr. McCloskey, and you wish an adjournment, we will, of course, consider the matter. But at least that shouldn't be a problem with starting with the examination-in-chief today, in any case. Yes, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I might maybe have my first declaration and then we will hear the witness later on, just to be available if it's easier for everyone. You know, I could just have my opening statement immediately after this witness if that suit the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's another possibility, and I thank you for the pragmatic way in which you make your proposal, Ms. Fauveau. Let's leave it. As I said, let's play it by the ear. We'll see how far we can go, if at all. But first priority is to finish with this witness now.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we will not have any cross-examination for this witness. However, should any issues arise after my learned friend's cross-examination, I will ask the Trial Chamber to give me some time for a few questions that I may have. I have reached this decision in consultation with my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. That's fair enough. Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ristivojevic.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon -- good evening, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You're probably right. My name is Peter Haynes, and together with Djordje Sarapa, I represent General Vinko Pandurevic, who in July of 1995 was Lieutenant Vinko Pandurevic, the commander of the Zvornik Brigade. I have a few areas to cross-examine you about, and you'll be comforted to hear they substantially involve regulations that you have already reviewed in your report. But what I may invite you to do is to apply those regulations to factual situations, which do or may arise in this case. And I trust you feel confident and able to do that given your experience and expertise. Do you?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we start, please, by considering what is our P409, the regulation on the applications of the International Laws of War in the armed forces of the Soviet [sic] Federative Republic of Yugoslavia.
